name: What is the R-value, and why is it important for attic insulation in Southern California?

mainEntity.name: What is the R-value, and why is it important for attic insulation in Southern California?

acceptedAnswer.text: The R-value measures thermal resistance, indicating how well insulation resists heat flow. A higher R-value means better insulating performance. For Southern California, while we primarily focus on keeping heat out, proper R-value is crucial for both cooling and heating efficiency. The recommended R-value for attics in our climate zone typically ranges from R-38 to R-60, depending on the specific construction and energy goals. Using the correct R-value prevents heat from entering during hot months and escaping during cooler periods, leading to optimal energy performance and comfort.
acceptedAnswer.description: R-value measures insulation's resistance to heat flow; a higher R-value improves energy efficiency. In Southern California, R-38 to R-60 is typically recommended to manage heat effectively.
